prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help you decide. I can also pull a short list of well-rated Pleasanton / Alameda‑County personal injury lawyers if you want — but first, here’s a practical, quick guide so you pick the right attorney for your car‑accident injury case.

Immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical care and follow doctors’ orders — your health and medical records are essential to the claim.
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries, witness contact info, and the police report number.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the at‑fault party’s insurer without a lawyer.
- Notify your insurer (if required) but be factual and brief.
- Note deadlines: in California the general personal‑injury statute of limitations is 2 years from the accident. Claims against public entities have much shorter notice deadlines (often 6 months).

How to choose the right lawyer
- Look for experience with car-accident personal injury cases (not just general practice).
- Ask about trial experience — lawyers who only settle may get lower offers from insurers.
- Local court knowledge (Alameda County and Pleasanton area) helps.
- Communication style and availability — you want someone who returns calls and explains things clearly.
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (you pay only if they recover). Typical contingency: ~33% for pre‑suit settlements; higher (often up to 40%) if a lawsuit is filed or an appeal is needed. Confirm who advances costs.
- Check credentials and reputation: State Bar record (no disciplinary issues), client reviews, peer ratings (Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers), trial verdicts/settlements.
- Meet (or have a video consult) with 2–3 lawyers to compare.

Questions to ask in the first meeting (phone or in person)
- How many car‑accident injury cases have you handled? How many in Alameda County?
- What percent of your cases settle vs go to trial? Do you try cases yourself?
- Who will handle my case day‑to‑day (partner, associate, paralegal)?
- What do you think my case is worth (range) and why?
- What is your fee rate and what costs will I be responsible for upfront or at the end?
- How do you communicate (phone/email/text)? How often will I get updates?
- Can you give references from past clients?
- Do you have experience with my specific injuries (neck, back, fractures, soft tissue, CT scans, MRIs)?

What to bring to that meeting
- Police report number and any photos of the crash or injuries.
- Medical records/bills, doctor names, dates of treatment.
- Insurance information (yours and other driver’s).
- Wage statements/time lost from work.
- Any correspondence with insurers or the other party.

Where to find and vet local attorneys
- California State Bar (attorney search) — check license and discipline history.
- Local reviews: Avvo, Super Lawyers, Martindale‑Hubbell, Google/Yelp.
- Local referrals: Ask your primary care doctor, friends, or coworkers in Pleasanton/Dublin/Livermore.
- Consider firms that advertise free consultations — use the meeting to compare.

When to hire one immediately
- Significant injuries, ongoing medical treatment, loss of work, unclear fault, the other driver is uninsured/underinsured, or insurers are pushing a quick low settlement.

If you want, I can:
- Find and list 3–5 well‑reviewed Pleasanton/Alameda County personal injury attorneys with short notes on experience and contact links.
- Or draft an email/phone script you can use when calling for initial consultations.

Which would you prefer? If you want a shortlist, tell me any preferences (trial lawyer vs. settlement‑focused, budget concerns, serious injury vs. minor).
